Following last week's ongoing 25% discount on AirPods Pro 3 and the $120 price cut on AirPods Max 2, today's main highlight at 9to5Toys Lunch is Amazon slashing the AirTag 2 to an all-time low, with the four-pack now selling for $80 (that's $20 each). Other deals include $320 off the Apple 24GB/1TB M5 MacBook Pro and $500 off this 2TB M5 Pro model. Don't miss Anker's brand-new SmartTrack Find My Wallet Card hitting an all-time low of $25 on Amazon, plus the LG 32-inch 6K Thunderbolt 5 monitor that's a whopping $2,200 cheaper than the Apple Studio Display XDR—also an all-time low. Read on for details.

AirPods Pro 3 still discounted 25%, next generation not expected until 2027

  • AirPods Pro 3 $190 (original price $249)
  • AirPods Max 2 $429 (original price $549)
  • AirPods 4 $99 (original price $129)

Ladies and gentlemen! AirTag 2 price drops again, four-pack now at an all-time low of $80 (that's $20 each)

Alright folks: Amazon is now offering the lowest price ever on the Apple 2026 AirTag 2 four-pack at just $20 per tag.

Amazon has now slashed the AirTag 2 four-pack to $79.99 with shipping.

Last week we were tracking this official pack at $89.99, then yesterday Amazon dropped it further to $85, and now Monday has opened with an even better price. Originally $99, it's now nearly 20% off—not the most dramatic deal in appearance, but a pretty solid discount for the latest AirTag 2.

At this pack price, each AirTag works out to just $20—the lowest price we've seen since it launched earlier this year.

The single AirTag 2 remains at the $24 Prime shipping price we saw last week, but the four-pack has set a new low (again).

Speaking of that $20-per-tag price, it matches last week's best open-box price we found at Best Buy—just throwing that out there.

Apple 24GB/1TB M5 MacBook Pro $320 off today, 2TB M5 Pro $500 off

Beyond the ongoing 25% discount on AirPods Pro 3 and the AirTag 2 hitting the lowest price we've tracked, this week also brings a few solid deals on the latest MacBook Pro lineup. Amazon still has the 2TB M5 Pro for $500 off, and we just spotted this more affordable M5 MacBook Pro 24GB model down $300. Details below.

If you want the more powerful M5 Pro, Amazon's $500-off model is absolutely worth a look. But if the base M5 is enough for you, B&H has a great deal on the 14-inch 24GB/1TB configuration:

B&H has once again dropped the Apple 14-inch M5 MacBook Pro with 24GB RAM and 1TB storage to $1,899 with shipping.

  • 14-inch M5 MacBook Pro 24GB/1TB $1,899 (original price $2,219)
  • Includes upgraded 96W Apple charger

This machine's original price is $2,199, but B&H throws in the original 96W Apple charger—which costs an extra $20 if configured on Apple's website.

Amazon currently prices the same MacBook Pro configuration at $2,049, including the standard 70W charger.

All in all, B&H's deal saves you $320 in total—on par with previously recommended offers and far more attractive than Amazon's pricing.

However, as mentioned, Amazon is still holding that massive discount on the 14-inch M5 Pro MacBook Pro 24GB/2TB at $2,699—$500 off the $3,199 original price—and it's unlikely to last long.

Anker's new SmartTrack Find My Wallet Card (supports iOS or Android) drops to an all-time low of $25 on Amazon

Anker recently launched its new SmartTrack Find My Wallet Card—the first product to support both Apple's tracking platform and Google's Find Hub—now down to an all-time low of $25 with Prime shipping on Amazon.

It debuted on Amazon last month at $35, then got a slight $5 trim by month's end, and now sees its first notable price drop, setting a new Amazon all-time low.

Nearly 30% off, matching the best deal we've tracked all year on similar wallet tracker cards.

Personally I'm a die-hard fan of Nomad Tracking Cards—the base version runs $35, and the Pro with 16-month battery life is $45—but regardless of which you choose, I think everyone should keep one in their wallet or cardholder. I never leave home without mine.

Anker's latest SmartTrack Card E40 has all the most important features, including wireless charging, and is compatible with both Apple Find My and Google Find Hub. At just 1.7mm thick with a ring volume of up to 80 decibels for easy nearby locating—and of course you can see its location on the map through the Find My and Find Hub apps.

Organize your desk with Anker's creative clamp-on power strip, now just $58

LG 32-inch 6K Thunderbolt 5 monitor drops to lowest price, a full $2,200 cheaper than Studio Display XDR

We just spotted B&H dropping the LG 32-inch UltraFine evo 6K monitor to $1,099.99 with shipping. Originally $2,000, and as high as $1,597 in recent months. This price essentially matches the all-time low set by Amazon earlier this month that's still in effect. LG's official store has also price-matched at $1,100 today, so there are options if one retailer is out of stock. At this price, the UltraFine evo 6K is significantly cheaper than Apple's offering. The Studio Display XDR starts at $3,299, making the LG 32-inch 6K Thunderbolt 5 monitor about $2,200 cheaper. Even the standard Studio Display starts at $1,549—saving you around $500—and you get a larger 32-inch 6K screen. Read on for details.

The LG 32-inch UltraFine evo 6K is a premium workstation monitor aimed at creators who want a large, high-resolution screen without paying Apple's premium prices. Its 6144 x 3456 display delivers over 21 million pixels at 224 PPI, giving you plenty of room to edit timelines, full-resolution content, tools, and multiple windows. Color coverage includes 99.5% Adobe RGB, with VESA DisplayHDR 600 support for better highlights and contrast. Connectivity is also comprehensive, including Thunderbolt 5, DisplayPort 2.1, HDMI, and USB-C. Mac users can also use LG Studio Mode and pre-calibrated color presets for more consistent creative work. All in all, it's a full-featured 6K option for users who want a truly large screen without paying Apple's monitor prices.

Woot also has some more affordable Samsung workstation monitor deals if you don't want to spend over $1,000 on a new display. Their M series and other budget-friendly models are now discounted, starting from $118.

Today's accessory and charging deals:

  • This ultra-thin UGREEN wallet tracker card works with iPhone and Android, now down to an all-time low of $20
  • This ultra-thin UGREEN 45W Nexode Air charger is the thinnest in my EDC, now just $27
  • Twelve South AirFly Pro wireless audio transmitter slashed to $40 on Amazon (black or white)
  • Chipolo Google Find Hub wallet card with super button/remote shutter feature, now down to $33
  • UGREEN MagFlow 25W Qi2.2 car charger back down to $28 (original price $40)
  • Acer metal MagSafe golf cart phone stand down to $20 with Prime shipping

Brand-new wireless Ring Battery Doorbell 4K Pro drops to Amazon all-time low, nearly 30% off (wired model also discounted)

As part of their late-summer promotion on Fire tablets, Fire TVs, and Blink smart home products, Amazon is also offering the best pricing ever on the new wireless Ring Battery Doorbell 4K Pro, and bringing the wired model back to its Prime Day all-time low—both at nearly 30% off list price.

  • Ring Battery Doorbell 4K Pro $180 (original price $250)
  • Ring Wired Doorbell 4K Pro $180 (original price $250)

While the brand later launched the more affordable Ring Peephole Cam 2K at $100, today's featured deals are some particularly impressive discounts on the latest Pro-tier 4K models.

The Ring Wired Doorbell 4K Pro is back at its Prime Day all-time low, returning for the first time since the big promo at the end of June. In fact, this is only the second time we've tracked this model below $200.

The wireless Ring Battery Doorbell 4K Pro sees its first-ever price drop, also setting an all-time low at $180.

As mentioned above, both models are priced at $250, so getting nearly 30% off is the best deal we've found—and the lowest price we've seen to date.

The two are largely similar, featuring up to 10x enhanced zoom, night vision, and Retinal 4K video with a wide-angle view for more detailed monitoring of your porch. The wireless model comes with a Quick Release Ultra battery pack for easy charging and simpler installation (no wiring required), while the wired model offers "unlimited power for around-the-clock protection."

For more details, check out our September unboxing coverage from last year.

Best Buy launches new tech deals, NFL Sunday Ticket promotion, and preseason TV deals

Amazon now has all five colors of AirPods Max 2 down $120 (one of the best prices ever)

This week's big 60th anniversary celebration brings one of the best prices yet on the Apple 2026 AirPods Max 2, with all five colors down $120 on Amazon.

Amazon has now dropped the Apple AirPods Max 2 to $429 with shipping.

Priced the same as the previous generation at $549, you save a full $120—the best pricing we've seen from reputable retailers on new stock.

Best Buy has the Midnight black version down to $403.99 with shipping, but it's "excellent" open-box condition—the lower price might not be enough to give up on new stock.

Apple launched a true next-generation AirPods Max this year, not just a new color and USB-C port. Unlike the in-ear AirPods line, next month's new releases shouldn't update its over-ear lineup, so this week might be your chance to snag Apple's latest and greatest over-ear headphones at $120 off for a while.

The only previous promo pricing lower than this was this summer's Prime Day, when it was marked $30 cheaper—but stock was tight during the four-day event.

Amazon selling this 512GB iPad mini at a new price with $450 off (Renewed Premium condition)

While we've started seeing some deals on the iPad Air this week, iPad discounts overall have been scarce lately, if any. That said, we just spotted Amazon dropping the latest 512GB iPad mini by $450 in Renewed Premium top-tier condition.

Amazon has now dropped the latest 512GB iPad mini A17 to $449 with shipping.

This pricing means getting $450 off Apple's $899 new iPad price, direct from Amazon.

Worth noting that even before the price drop, we've never seen this model go below $679 for new stock on Amazon.

Quick reminder: Amazon's Renewed Premium tier is different from regular renewed or "excellent" condition refurbished units. Its shipping specs are as follows:

  • Screen: If equipped with a screen, the screen has no scratches whatsoever.
  • Body: When viewed from 12 inches away, the body has no visible cosmetic damage (scratches, dents, etc.).
  • Battery: If equipped with a battery, its capacity exceeds 90% of the original battery life.
  • Accessories: Comes with generic or original accessories and packaging.
  • Guarantee: Renewed Premium items come with a 365-day return window.

Amazon's highest quality Premium Renewed iPhone 17 Pro models down $220 today (matching Prime Day deal)

While Apple's official certified refurbished store is my first stop for iPhone deals, Apple isn't currently selling the latest iPhone 17 Pro models there—looks like we'll have to wait until after next month's 18 series launches. Amazon's highest quality Premium Renewed stock is now back at Prime Day pricing, with up to $220 off.

Amazon's top-tier Premium Renewed stock has consistently been the most affordable way to get an unlocked iPhone 17 Pro. You save hundreds of dollars and get a 1-year Amazon Renewed guarantee plus "over 90% of original battery life" quality—non-"Premium" renewed and refurbished items only come with a 90-day warranty and lesser battery life.

Right now you can find 1TB and 512GB iPhone 17 Pro models back at this price, with up to $220 off—the 512GB version is another $20 cheaper than last time we featured it:

  • 1TB iPhone 17 Pro Cosmic Orange $1,279 (original $1,499 new)
  • 1TB iPhone 17 Pro Deep Blue $1,279 (original $1,499 new)
  • 1TB iPhone 17 Pro Silver $1,279 (original $1,499 new)
  • 512GB iPhone 17 Pro Cosmic Orange $1,179 (original $1,299 new)
  • 512GB iPhone 17 Pro Deep Blue $1,179 (original $1,299 new)
  • 512GB iPhone 17 Pro Silver $1,179 (original $1,299 new)

As detailed in yesterday's Apple refurbished store curated picks, you can get a perfectly capable iPhone 16 model starting from $699 with a 1-year Apple warranty; the 1TB 16 Pro Max at $1,269—$330 cheaper than the equivalent 17 Pro Max, and $130 cheaper than the 512GB 17 Pro.

  • Refurbished iPhone 16 from $699 (up to $330 cheaper than the 17 series)
